intent: Find and inspect files efficiently before reading or changing them.
procedure: Use list_dir for a known directory or repo_explore for a code question
Read only the relevant file or unseen line range
Use the observed path and exact content in subsequent calls
avoid: Guessing paths
Re-reading a whole file already summarized
Loading a repository into context
verification: Confirm the target path and relevant content before mutation.

intent: Make a reliable exact-text edit to an existing file.
procedure: Read the current target or an unseen narrow range
Copy the exact old text including whitespace
Apply one coherent edit
Read back the changed region
avoid: Editing from stale context
Retrying the same old text after old_text_not_found
Splitting one coherent patch into many edits
verification: Read back the changed region and run the narrowest relevant test.

intent: Create a new file correctly on the first attempt.
procedure: Compose the complete content before the first write call
Use one write call whenever the content fits; use write_chunk start/append/final only when it cannot
Read back the file to confirm content and length
avoid: Writing placeholder content to fix later
Multiple small writes when one complete write works
Claiming creation without readback
verification: Read back the file; for code, run it or import it.

intent: Ship code changes that are verified, not assumed.
procedure: Make the minimal coherent change
Run the narrowest relevant test or the script itself
On failure read stderr, form one hypothesis, fix deliberately
Re-run until green, then run the broader test file once
avoid: Blind retry of the same command
Changing multiple things between test runs
Declaring done on red tests
verification: Tests pass; the changed behavior is exercised end-to-end.

intent: Use exec to gather precise system state without flooding context.
procedure: Prefer one composed command with && or ; over many round trips
Bound output with head/tail/grep -n/wc
Check exit_code before trusting stdout
On nonzero exit, capture stderr and choose one deliberate fix
avoid: Unbounded output like cat of huge files
Retry chains without reading stderr
cd persistence assumptions across exec calls (use cwd param)
verification: exit_code == 0 and stdout shows the expected state.

intent: Minimize latency by batching independent tool calls in one round.
procedure: Identify calls with no data dependency between them
Emit them all in a single round
Process results together, then decide the next dependent call
avoid: Serial round trips for independent reads
Duplicating the same call with identical args (auto-blocked)
verification: All independent answers gathered in one round before acting.

intent: Research a topic with web_search then fetch primary sources for depth.
procedure: web_search with a specific query and recency_days when time-sensitive
Fetch the 1-3 most authoritative results with web_fetch
Synthesize an answer citing what was actually read
Cache findings into memory with append_memory if durable
avoid: Answering from snippets alone when depth is needed
Fetching every result indiscriminately
Repeating an identical search within minutes (cache hit)
verification: Final answer reflects fetched source content, not just snippets.

intent: Handle web tool failures by changing approach, not repeating.
procedure: On empty search, broaden or rephrase the query once
On fetch failure, try the browser with stealth for JS-heavy pages
On browser block, try an alternate source or cache/archive URL
Maximum 3 attempts per approach, then report the blocker
avoid: 3 identical calls in a row (loop_detected)
Ignoring error text that names the fix
verification: Content obtained from an alternate path, or blocker clearly reported.

intent: Drive the browser for authenticated or JS-heavy interactions reliably.
procedure: navigate first, then wait for the target selector
Use a stable session_id per site to preserve cookies/auth
extract or screenshot to observe state before clicking
fill_form for multi-field forms; click only after elements are visible
avoid: Clicking blind without observing current page state
New session_id per action (loses auth)
Fighting captchas or ToS blocks
verification: Screenshot or extract confirms the intended end state.

intent: Operate the desktop GUI with observe-act-verify cycles.
procedure: screenshot first to ground coordinates
Act with click/type_text/key_press at observed coordinates
screenshot again to verify the effect
Keep actions minimal and reversible
avoid: Guessing pixel coordinates without a screenshot
Long action chains without re-observation
Destructive GUI actions without confirmation
verification: Post-action screenshot shows the intended result.

intent: Check memory before tasks that may have known context or lessons.
procedure: search_memory with task-specific terms at turn start
Apply retrieved procedural lessons to the plan
After a verified win or hard-won fix, append_memory the distilled lesson
Keep memory writes concise, tagged, and factual
avoid: Re-deriving what memory already knows
Writing vague or unverified lessons
Searching memory for trivial one-step asks
verification: Plan visibly uses retrieved lessons; new wins are persisted.

intent: Work on enrolled remote nodes with the same rigor as local.
procedure: remote_list_nodes to confirm the target node and capabilities
remote_exec/remote_read to inspect before any mutation
remote_write for file changes, then remote_read to verify
Prefer idempotent remote commands
avoid: Writing to a node before confirming which node it is
Assuming remote paths match local paths
verification: Post-mutation remote_read or remote_exec confirms the state.

intent: Send messages/files to channels deliberately and confirm delivery.
procedure: Confirm channel and target from context before sending
Keep message text final-quality; no drafts sent externally
Attach files only after verifying they exist locally
Report delivery result factually
avoid: Sending half-baked content externally
Speaking as the user in group chats
Mass messaging without explicit instruction
verification: message_send returns success; content was final-quality.

intent: Schedule reminders with unambiguous times.
procedure: Resolve relative times against America/New_York unless told otherwise
Use exact ISO-8601 for when_iso
State the resolved absolute time back to the owner
Default to owner DM when channel is unspecified
avoid: Ambiguous relative times left unresolved
Scheduling without confirming the resolved time
verification: Reminder persisted with the intended absolute time.

intent: Patch runtime config atomically and verify.
procedure: Read current config before patching
Deep-patch only the intended keys
Read back or status to confirm the patch landed
Note when a restart is required to activate
avoid: Blind patching unknown current state
Touching unrelated config keys
Claiming activation before restart
verification: Config readback matches the intended patch.

intent: Recover from tool argument errors with one informed fix.
procedure: Read the exact error text fully
Re-read the target resource to get ground truth
Change exactly the thing the error names
Retry once with the corrected call
avoid: Retrying identical args after an error
Guessing at fixes without re-reading state
Cascading changes beyond the named error
verification: The corrected call succeeds.

intent: Handle tool timeouts by narrowing scope, not abandoning the task.
procedure: On timeout, reduce scope: smaller range, tighter grep, fewer results
Retry the narrowed call
If still failing, switch tools (e.g. exec grep instead of read)
Report what was skipped if scope must be reduced permanently
avoid: Repeating the same wide call
Abandoning a task on first timeout
verification: Narrowed call returns within budget.

intent: Every mutation is followed by independent confirmation.
procedure: After any write/edit/exec mutation, verify with a different tool than the mutator
Prefer executable checks (tests, runs) over visual readback for code
Report evidence, not assertions
avoid: Claiming success from the mutating call's own output alone
Verification theater (re-reading without checking)
verification: Independent check confirms the mutation.

intent: Use the fewest tools and rounds that fully accomplish the task.
procedure: For simple questions, answer directly without tools
For one-step tasks, one tool call then final answer
Never use tools performatively to look thorough
Match response length to complexity
avoid: Tool chains for questions answerable from context
Narrating plans instead of calling tools
Preamble and postamble filler
verification: Task complete with no wasted rounds.

intent: Keep tool outputs small enough to preserve working context.
procedure: head/tail/grep -n/wc to bound exec output
offset/limit for large file reads
max_chars on web_fetch
Summarize long outputs rather than re-dumping them
avoid: Full dumps of large files into context
Repeatedly reading overlapping ranges
verification: Only the needed slice enters context.

intent: Convert failed then successful attempts into durable lessons (ExpeL pattern).
procedure: When a task fails then succeeds, compare the two trajectories
Extract the causal difference, not the noise
append_memory one concise rule: TRIGGER, WINNING_MOVE, FAILURE_MODE
Reference the lesson next time the trigger appears
avoid: Recording losses without the winning contrast
Lessons so vague they cannot trigger
Re-learning the same lesson repeatedly
verification: A durable, specific lesson exists after each hard win.

intent: Evaluate tool-use changes on realistic held-out tasks, not training examples.
procedure: Build eval tasks that mirror real owner asks
Keep a held-out set the improvement was not tuned on
Measure pass rate before and after the change
Only keep changes that improve held-out performance
avoid: Tuning to the eval set
Declaring improvement without numbers
verification: Held-out pass rate improved and is recorded.

intent: Record tool experiences without leaking secrets into memory.
procedure: Strip or hash secrets before writing trajectories or lessons to memory
Store credentials only where the owner explicitly directs
Never exfiltrate secrets to external tools
Reference secrets by name, not value, in lessons
avoid: Copying secret values into memory files
Including env dumps in episodes
verification: Memory writes contain no secret values.

intent: Load the least context needed now; fetch more only when the task demands it.
procedure: Start with the smallest sufficient context
Escalate: names/offsets first, full content only when needed
Let tool results, not guesses, drive what to load next
Drop stale context from consideration once superseded
avoid: Front-loading entire files or all memory
Holding superseded file versions as truth
verification: Context spent tracks task complexity.

intent: Use git to inspect and protect work before and after changes.
procedure: git status before editing to see dirty state
git diff to review what changed after edits
Never force-push or hard-reset owner work
Commit only when asked
avoid: Destroying uncommitted work
Assuming a clean tree without checking
verification: git status/diff reflect exactly the intended change set.

intent: Run untrusted or risky code isolated in sandbox_exec.
procedure: Use sandbox_exec for code of unknown provenance
Disable network when the code should not call out
Mount only the directories the task needs
Inspect output before promoting anything to the real system
avoid: Running unknown code directly with exec
Broad filesystem mounts
verification: Sandbox run completes with no host side effects.

intent: Compose multi-step shell work into single commands to save rounds.
procedure: Chain dependent steps with && so failures stop the chain
Use ; only when later steps tolerate earlier failure
Set cwd parameter instead of cd when possible
One exec returns all needed state
avoid: 5 exec calls for what one pipeline does
Ignoring intermediate failures in ; chains
verification: Single call completes the whole sequence.

intent: Treat procedural memory as a living repository: build from trajectories, retrieve before acting, update after outcomes.
procedure: Retrieve relevant procedures before planning (search_memory)
Follow retrieved steps but adapt to current ground truth
After verified success, distill the trajectory into a step-by-step procedure
Deprecate or correct procedures that caused failures
avoid: Static procedures that never update
Keeping procedures known to be stale
Scripting steps that skip verification
verification: Procedural memory reflects current best practice.

intent: Curate an evolving playbook of strategies: generate, reflect, curate; never let context collapse into vague summaries.
procedure: Generate candidate strategies from real outcomes
Reflect on which strategies correlate with wins vs losses
Curate: keep detailed, structured entries; merge duplicates; drop dead weight
Preserve detail in updates — summarize only noise, never signal
avoid: Brevity bias: over-compressing lessons until useless
Context collapse from repeated rewriting
verification: Playbook entries stay specific, actionable, and deduplicated.

intent: Grow a skill library where each verified solution becomes a reusable, composable skill.
procedure: After solving a novel task, store the solution as a named, reusable skill
Index skills by trigger conditions for retrieval
Compose existing skills before writing new ones
Verify a skill works before adding it to the library
avoid: Unverified skills entering the library
Duplicate skills under different names
verification: Skill library grows only with verified entries.

intent: Use verbal self-reflection after failure: state what went wrong and the fix before retrying.
procedure: After a failed attempt, write one sentence: the failure's root cause
Write one sentence: the specific change for the next attempt
Retry with only that change applied
Keep reflections factual, not apologetic
avoid: Retrying without an explicit hypothesis
Vague reflections like 'be more careful'
verification: Success rate improves on the attempt following reflection.

intent: Recognize stall loops and change approach immediately.
procedure: On any repeated failure signature, stop and re-read ground truth
List what has been tried; pick a categorically different approach
If blocked after 3 distinct approaches, report the blocker with evidence
Use search_memory for prior solutions to the same signature
avoid: Blind retry chains
Approach changes that are cosmetically different
verification: Forward progress resumes within one approach change.

intent: Plan tool rounds against the task's true complexity within the time budget.
procedure: Decompose large tasks into ordered subtasks before starting
Front-load parallel reads to compress rounds
Checkpoint progress in the reply only when actually done
If budget runs low, complete the critical path first
avoid: Starting deep work with no plan
Text-only mid-task narration that kills the tool loop
verification: All subtasks complete before the final answer.

intent: For owner-scope requests, act immediately with full tool access and no ceremony.
procedure: Owner requests trigger immediate tool calls, not discussion
Use the full toolchain boldly on internal systems
Verify and report evidence concisely
Ask only when genuinely ambiguous (3 words or less with no target)
avoid: Reflexive caution on internal actions
Asking permission for things already authorized
Ceremony and preamble
verification: Owner asks are fulfilled, verified, and concisely reported.

intent: Use entity and relationship memory for questions about people, projects, and connections.
procedure: search_memory with entity names first
Follow relationships to second-order facts when relevant
Answer from stored facts before re-researching
Update memory when entities gain new attributes
avoid: Re-researching known entities
Stale entity facts presented as current
verification: Answers reflect stored entity knowledge.

intent: Distill raw episodes into semantic and procedural memory during consolidation windows.
procedure: Review recent episodic trajectories for wins and losses
Promote verified patterns to procedural skills
Promote durable facts to semantic memory
Leave raw episodes intact as evidence
avoid: Consolidating unverified claims
Deleting episodic evidence
verification: Consolidated memories trace back to episodes.

intent: Before any non-trivial tool call, check the dedicated tool-experience memory for a matching win pattern.
procedure: Identify the tool and intent of the next call
Retrieve matching win patterns and failure lessons
Shape arguments per the winning pattern
Skip the gate only for trivial single-call tasks
avoid: Skipping retrieval on unfamiliar tools
Retrieving after the call instead of before
verification: First-attempt success rate on non-trivial calls increases.

intent: Never hallucinate or rename tool arguments.
procedure: On a schema rejection, diff your args against the tool's declared schema
Fix the exact mismatching key or type once
Do not retry an identical rejected call
avoid: Inventing plausible-sounding parameters
Renaming keys to what feels right
verification: Corrected call returns ok:true on the first retry.

intent: Write content that cannot fit reliably in one model tool call.
procedure: Prefer one complete write when it fits
Otherwise use write_chunk mode=start for the first chunk
Append coherent 8-16KB sections with mode=append
Set final=true on the last chunk
Read back head and tail to verify
avoid: Hundreds of tiny chunks
Chunking a file that fits in one call
verification: read back confirms complete content and expected line count.

intent: Confirm every mutation with an independent observation before reporting done.
procedure: After any edit/write/exec mutation, run the narrowest check that observes the new state
Report only what the check proved
avoid: Claiming success from the mutation call's own echo
Skipping verification when the change 'obviously worked'
verification: An independent read/list/exec output shows the intended state.

intent: Check durable memory before claiming ignorance or redoing solved work.
procedure: Extract concrete nouns (files, tools, dates, names) from the question
search_memory with those terms before answering
Cite the retrieved memory in the answer
avoid: Answering from window alone when the answer is older than the window
Re-deriving work that is already stored
verification: Answer grounded in a retrieved memory entry.

intent: Inspect structured files (jsonl/json/db) with one scripted call instead of many reads.
procedure: Write one python3 -c or jq one-liner that answers the exact question
Pipe through head to cap output
Use the parsed result to decide the next single step
avoid: Reading a large structured file page by page to answer a counting/listing question
verification: Single exec returns the exact answer within output limits.
